API Reference

Flask Application

Flask analysis webpage for Module 4.

app.create_app(config=None, session_factory=None, analysis_query=None, pull_runner=None)[source]

Create and configure the Grad Cafe Flask application.

Dependencies may be injected during testing so tests do not need live scraping, LLM calls, or a production database.

Database Models

SQLAlchemy ORM models for the Grad Cafe database.

These classes map to the existing PostgreSQL tables. Running this file does not create, delete, or modify tables.

ORM Queries

Module 3: SQLAlchemy ORM Query Analysis

Reproduce the nine required SQL questions and two original questions using SQLAlchemy ORM queries.

The underlying PostgreSQL tables are not modified.

Match admission statuses beginning with ‘accept’.

Data Loading

Module 3: Load cleaned Grad Cafe applicant data into PostgreSQL.

Run from the module_3 folder:

python load_data.py

PostgreSQL connection settings come from environment variables. No database password is stored in this file.

load_data.clean_url(value)[source]

Extract the URL from either plain text or a Markdown link.

load_data.connect_to_database()[source]

Connect using the environment variables set in PowerShell.

load_data.get_applicant_id(record, position)[source]

Use the numeric Grad Cafe result ID from the applicant’s URL.

This gives each applicant a stable p_id rather than assigning an ID based on their position in the JSON file.

load_data.main()[source]
load_data.optional_date(value)[source]

Convert dates such as ‘Sep 12, 2026’ to Python date objects.

load_data.optional_number(value)[source]

Convert a score to a float, or return NULL if it is missing.

load_data.optional_text(value)[source]

Convert blank or missing text to a database NULL.

load_data.prepare_record(record, position)[source]

Map one JSON record to the required PostgreSQL columns.

load_data.verify_table_columns(cursor)[source]

Stop if an existing applicants table has a different schema.

Load original downloaded university names into a supplementary table.

The required 15-column applicants table remains unchanged.

Query Analysis

Module 3: SQL Query Analysis

Answers the nine required SQL questions using PostgreSQL and Psycopg 3.

All analysis is performed in SQL. Python executes the queries and formats their results for console output.

query_data.connect_to_database()[source]

Connect to PostgreSQL using environment variables.

query_data.fetch_one(connection, sql)[source]

Execute a SQL query and return its first result row.

query_data.format_average(value)[source]

Format an average to two decimal places.

query_data.format_percentage(value)[source]

Format a percentage to two decimal places.

query_data.main()[source]

Run all eleven SQL analysis questions.

Page Capture

capture_page.capture_pages(web_mode=False)[source]

Capture a batch of ordinary public GradCafe pages.

Cloudflare verification remains manual. The program stops rather than bypassing verification/blocking.

Data Cleaning

Clean GradCafe records using the local standardization LLM.

clean.clean_data(input_file=WindowsPath('C:/Users/wedne/jhu_software_concepts/module_4/src/applicant_data.json'), output_file=WindowsPath('C:/Users/wedne/jhu_software_concepts/module_4/src/llm_extend_applicant_data.json'), llm_caller=None)[source]

Standardize GradCafe program and university values.

Parameters:

  • input_file (pathlib.Path or str) – Raw applicant JSON file.

  • output_file (pathlib.Path or str) – Cleaned applicant JSON file.

  • llm_caller (callable, optional) – Function used to standardize a record. Tests may inject a fake function so no real LLM or network dependency is required.

Returns:

Cleaned applicant records.

Return type:

list

clean.load_data(path)[source]

Load JSON data from a file.

clean.save_data(data, path)[source]

Save JSON data to a file.
